account: AVCI (Açık Kaynak İstihbaratı Analiz Sistemi, Open Source Intelligence Analysis System) is an AI-supported program. The Istanbul Police Department's narcotics and cybercrime divisions built it in-house with a special software team. Police chief Selami Yıldız ordered the work. It infiltrates closed groups and channels on end-to-end encrypted messaging apps. It analyzes messages, voice notes, photos and location data. It also decodes dealer slang, links profiles and maps group relationships. By copying traffic to its own servers while the traffic is accessible, it preserves material that users later delete. Police first used AVCI on 10 February 2026, in a drug operation that was centered on Istanbul and ran across 14 provinces. Anadolu Agency reported that day that the simultaneous raids had taken place that morning in 14 provinces and 35 districts and that 305 of 346 sought suspects had been detained. On 13 February 2026 the Istanbul Chief Public Prosecutor's Office said that 324 suspects had been caught, 21 of them group administrators, and that criminal judgeships of peace had remanded all of them. Anadolu Agency reported on 6 April 2026 that 325 suspects had been detained in the operation. All 325 referred to court were remanded in custody. 69 messaging-app groups were closed.

ai_role.statement: By the police account relayed by Anadolu Agency, AVCI infiltrated closed messaging groups and decoded slang and coded language. It preserved messages by recording group traffic before users deleted it, linked profiles through IP analysis, and mapped group relationships. That work produced the suspects and groups targeted on 10 February. Police and courts carried out the detentions, referrals and remands. The sources include no independent evaluation of the system. No official is quoted on how many of the 325 were identified by AVCI rather than by conventional work. The sources name no developer beyond the police's own software team.

fields.account: AVCI (Açık Kaynak İstihbaratı Analiz Sistemi, Open Source Intelligence Analysis System) is an AI-supported program. The Istanbul Police Department's narcotics and cybercrime divisions built it in-house with a special software team. Police chief Selami Yıldız ordered the work. It infiltrates closed groups and channels on end-to-end encrypted messaging apps. It analyzes messages, voice notes, photos and location data. It also decodes dealer slang, links profiles and maps group relationships. By copying traffic to its own servers while the traffic is accessible, it preserves material that users later delete. Police first used AVCI on 10 February 2026, in a drug operation that was centered on Istanbul and ran across 14 provinces. Anadolu Agency reported that day that the simultaneous raids had taken place that morning in 14 provinces and 35 districts and that 305 of 346 sought suspects had been detained. On 13 February 2026 the Istanbul Chief Public Prosecutor's Office said that 324 suspects had been caught, 21 of them group administrators, and that criminal judgeships of peace had remanded all of them. Anadolu Agency reported on 6 April 2026 that 325 suspects had been detained in the operation. All 325 referred to court were remanded in custody. 69 messaging-app groups were closed.
